findings.title: Headline distribution-preserving subject split not implemented in repo
findings.claim: The only in-repo cross-validation splitter (`data_splitting.py`, cv branch) partitions the unique patients with a plain `KFold` and, at lines 28-30, warns the user it 'does not preserve the BP distributions between the folds' and to 'refer to Figshare split datasets or Scientific Data paper for self-implementation'. No code performs the paper's iterative multi-label stratification (confirmed absent by `_audit_code/check_missing_gen_code.py`).
findings.concern: The paper's central methodological contribution — a subject-level split that also preserves the joint SBP/DBP distribution via iterative stratification for multi-label data — has no implementation in the repository, so the split procedure cannot be reproduced or verified from the code (only the resulting Figshare splits are provided).
findings.resolution: Authors: please release the iterative-stratification split-generation script (the code that produced the `label_class`/`agg_ohe` columns and the Figshare `*_fold` files), or confirm the fold files are the sole artefact.
findings.paper_ref: Methods — 'Validation strategies' (iterative stratification for multi-label data)

findings.title: Feature-importance computation (RF + Extra-Trees, Gini) absent; only pickles shipped
findings.quote: The feature importance is the normalized mean decrease of the Gini impurity achieved across the ensembles.
findings.claim: The training pipeline loads precomputed importances from `feat_importance/<dataset>/featImportance-{SP,DP}.pkl` (`core/loaders/feat_loader.py:94-101`) and selects the top `rate_features` fraction, but no code in the repo trains the fully-grown RF + Extra-Trees (500 trees) ensembles or computes the Gini importances (no `RandomForest`/`ExtraTrees`/`feature_importances_` anywhere — see `_audit_code/check_missing_gen_code.py`).
findings.concern: Fig. 3 and the Results claims about which PPG feature subgroups/individual features are most important rest entirely on eight precomputed pickle files whose generating procedure is not in the repo, so the feature-selection step and its ranking cannot be reproduced or audited.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the script that fits the RF/Extra-Trees ensembles and writes the `featImportance-*.pkl` files, so the importance ranking (and Fig. 3) is reproducible.
findings.paper_ref: Methods — Feat2Lab feature selection; Results — 'Feature importance in Feat2Lab models'

findings.title: No code for Fig. 2 significance (bootstrap+Bonferroni) or Fig. 4/5 experiments
findings.quote: The custom code used for data visualization is available from the corresponding authors upon request.
findings.claim: The comparative conclusions rest on Fig. 2 (bootstrap confidence intervals and Bonferroni-corrected pairwise significance lines) and on the Fig. 4 (leak vs no-leak) and Fig. 5 (distribution before/after) experiments; a repo-wide grep finds no bootstrap/Bonferroni/significance/leak-experiment code (`_audit_code/check_missing_gen_code.py` and grep for `bootstrap|bonferroni|wilcoxon|significan|leak` return nothing). The code-availability statement defers this code to 'upon request'.
findings.concern: The paper's headline model-ranking claims ('SVR/ResNet/U-Net significantly outperforms ...') and its two leakage/distribution demonstrations cannot be reproduced or verified from the repository; 'available on request' is not a resolvable artefact.
findings.resolution: Authors: please release the significance-testing code (bootstrap CIs + Bonferroni comparisons for Fig. 2) and the Fig. 4/Fig. 5 experiment scripts, rather than providing them only on request.

findings.title: Early-stopping patience is 10 in every DL config; paper states 15
findings.claim: Every deep-learning config sets `param_early_stop.patience: 10` (all 24 `dl/**` configs; verified by grep), whereas the Methods section states early stopping used a patience of 15 epochs on the validation loss.
findings.concern: A shorter early-stopping patience than reported can change which epoch/checkpoint is selected and thus the reported DL numbers, though the effect is small and both values are individually valid; the discrepancy is a faithfulness mismatch, not a leak (monitor is validation, `mode min`).
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the patience actually used for the reported DL results (paper says 15, configs say 10) and reconcile the configs or the text.
findings.paper_ref: Methods — 'Hyperparameter tuning' ('early stopping with the patience of 15 epochs in the validation loss')

findings.title: Hydra/Optuna tuning objective is the TEST-fold MAE, not validation
findings.claim: Both hyperparameter-search entrypoints return the aggregated TEST-fold MAE as the value Optuna minimizes: `tune.py:100` returns `cv_metrics["test/sbp_mae"]` and `tune_ml.py:97` returns `cv_metrics[f"ts/{target}_mae"]`; the Optuna sweeper is `direction: minimize` (`core/config/tune/ml/lgb_sensors_SP.yaml:22`). `solver.evaluate()` also computes a validation aggregate (`val/..._mae`) that is available to return instead. Cached-run reuse is likewise keyed on the test MAE (`tune.py:59-61`, `tune_ml.py:57-60`). Verified by `_audit_code/check_tuning_objective.py`.
findings.concern: Hyperparameters are chosen to minimize error on exactly the folds whose error is reported as the benchmark result, so Table 2's test MAE/ME/SD/MASE are optimistically biased by test-set model selection — contradicting the paper's own statement that tuning monitored 'the MAE performance of validation sets' and undermining the benchmark's purpose of fair comparison.
findings.resolution: Authors: change the tuning objective to the validation aggregate (`val/..._mae`) and re-run the search, or confirm whether the Table 2 configs' hyperparameters were in fact selected by this test-minimizing search; report the gap between validation-selected and test-selected results.
findings.paper_ref: Methods — 'Hyperparameter tuning' ('monitoring the MAE performance of validation sets')
